prompt: A delivery van moves along a straight horizontal road to the right. The driver applies the brakes, causing the van to decelerate uniformly. Which row correctly gives the directions of the velocity, resultant force, and acceleration of the van?
options: velocity: to the right; resultant force: to the right; acceleration: to the right
velocity: to the right; resultant force: to the left; acceleration: to the left
velocity: to the right; resultant force: to the left; acceleration: to the right
velocity: to the left; resultant force: to the left; acceleration: to the right

answer.explanation: Velocity is to the right because the van moves to the right. Since it is slowing down, resultant force and acceleration both act to the left.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 describes a vehicle speeding up to the right, not decelerating.

Option 2 is correct. The van travels to the right, so velocity points right. Deceleration means acceleration opposes velocity (points left). Resultant force always shares the direction of acceleration (points left).
Option 3 violates Newton's second law by showing acceleration opposite to resultant force.
Option 4 incorrectly states that the van is moving to the left.
hints: Velocity indicates the instantaneous direction of motion.
Deceleration means acceleration is directed opposite to the direction of motion.
Resultant force and acceleration always point in the exact same direction.
solution: Velocity points to the right (direction of motion). Deceleration means acceleration points to the left. Acceleration and resultant force always share the same direction, so resultant force also points to the left. Option B is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Emphasize the difference between direction of motion (velocity) and direction of change in motion (acceleration).
Because the vehicle slows down, acceleration must oppose velocity.
Reinforce the fundamental rule: acceleration and resultant force always have identical directions.
